title: Calculation Sheet — The Late Report Penalty
content:
**Calculation.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, a late report penalty is owed for every quarterly contribution and wage report filed after its due date, and it is worked out from the original report with the latest filing date on the account. The late report penalty is the larger of the class's flat late report penalty and the class's late report percentage of that report's total wages, limited by the class's late report penalty maximum, and rounded to the cent.

| Element | Source |
|---|---|
| Report | The original report with the latest filing date on the account; its quarter is the quarter the penalty is booked for |
| Total wages | The total wages shown on that report (total wages, not taxable wages) |
| Flat late report penalty, late report percentage, penalty maximum | Figures of the account's financing class |
| Rounding | To the cent, once, on the amount booked |

## Worked figures (hypothetical reports, with class figures of USD 50.00 flat, 0.001 of total wages and a USD 250.00 maximum)

| Total wages on the report | Percentage of total wages | Larger of that and the flat penalty | After the maximum | Penalty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30,000.00 | 30.00 | 50.00 | 50.00 | USD 50.00 |
| 180,000.00 | 180.00 | 180.00 | 180.00 | USD 180.00 |
| 400,000.00 | 400.00 | 400.00 | 250.00 | USD 250.00 |
| 123,456.78 | 123.45678 | 123.45678 | 123.45678 | USD 123.46 |

## Points of judgement

- **Where the flat amount and the percentage meet.** With total wages of USD 50,000.00 the percentage gives exactly 50.00, the same as the flat amount; the penalty is USD 50.00 either way.
- **Where the percentage meets the maximum.** With total wages of USD 250,000.00 the percentage gives exactly 250.00; any higher wages still give USD 250.00.
- **Which report.** If the employer filed an original report for one quarter on 12 May and another original report for a different quarter on 3 June, the penalty is worked out from the report filed on 3 June.
